text.zh: 现生成员包括马、犀和貘。承重轴经过第三指（趾），但不能据此把所有成员说成只有奇数个趾：貘的前足有四趾。它们通过后肠发酵利用植物性食物。
text.en: Living members include horses, rhinoceroses and tapirs. The weight-bearing axis passes through the third digit; this does not mean every foot has an odd number of toes, since tapir forefeet have four. Plant food is processed by hindgut fermentation.

text.en: Living equids include horses, asses and zebras. An enlarged third digit and hoof support the foot, and high-crowned cheek teeth process abrasive food. This living single-toed condition must not be assigned to every fossil equid.

text.en: Living rhinoceroses have robust limbs, normally with three digits on each foot. Their horns are made of keratin. Feeding ranges from browsing to grazing; one species does not represent the ecology of the entire family.

text.en: A mobile short proboscis formed by the nose and upper lip grasps vegetation. Forefeet have four digits and hindfeet three; cheek teeth bear transverse ridges. Juvenile stripes and spots should not be used as adult identification characters.

text.en: This genus includes horses, asses and zebras. Hooves and high-crowned cheek teeth support terrestrial movement and processing plant food, while water needs, social organization and habitats differ among species.

text.en: This catalogue places lowland and mountain tapirs in this genus. The lowland tapir has a short mane along the head and neck; that observation belongs to the species and is not a universal description of all tapirs.

text.en: Mountain tapirs inhabit Andean cloud forests and high-elevation grasslands. Dense fur and pale lip margins are useful features. A broad habitat account does not establish occurrence at every locality.

text.en: A single horn and pronounced skin folds are characteristic. This species uses alluvial grasslands, wetlands and adjacent woodland. Habitat use depends on water, food and disturbance; historical range is not equivalent to current occupancy.

text.en: The pointed, mobile upper lip gathers browse, unlike the white rhino’s broad mouth. Adhering soil affects apparent colour, so colour alone does not reliably distinguish black and white rhinoceroses.

text.en: Small among living rhinoceroses, this species has conspicuous hair and two horns; calves have a denser coat. Forest accounts describe morphology and habitat but do not substitute for a current population census.

text.en: A broad, roughly square mouth suits feeding on grasses near ground level, and the neck and shoulders form a prominent hump. A species overview does not erase taxonomic debate or differing conservation circumstances of northern and southern populations.

text.en: African wild asses should be distinguished from domestic donkeys. This biological source concerns Somali wild asses, including striped legs and feeding in arid habitats; subspecies traits are not automatically generalized to all African wild asses.

text.en: A throat dewlap and rump stripe pattern help comparison with other zebras. Mountain habitats and climbing ability are relevant to its ecology; all zebras should not be assigned a single plains-herding pattern.

text.en: A stocky body and upright mane without the domestic horse’s long forelock are characteristic. It feeds on plants, and conservation includes breeding and reintroduction. Relationships with early human-managed horses require ancient-genome evidence.

text.en: Plains zebras use African grasslands and open woodland and feed mainly on grasses. Stripe patterns vary within the species. This entry concerns the entire species; extinction of the quagga must not be assigned to all Equus quagga.

text.en: A dark dorsal stripe and pale underside are typical, with coat colour varying by season and region. Grasses and other plant material are eaten. Species-level summaries do not replace subspecies or population distributions.

text.en: Narrow stripes, large rounded ears and a largely white belly are characteristic. Semi-arid grasslands are important habitat, and water needs vary with reproductive state. Its social organization should not simply be copied from plains-zebra family groups.
